title: Special Edition: The Reincarnated One Who Was Reincarnated as a Reincarnated One
text: “No way…”

When I suddenly came to, I found myself in a room in a strange mansion. I looked around, wondering what on earth was going on. There was no doubt about it—I was overcome by a strange sensation: it felt vaguely familiar, yet at the same time, like I’d never seen this place before.

And there I was, wearing jeans and a jacket I didn’t remember putting on… I was even more surprised to see that my hair wasn’t the color I knew it to be. What the hell is going on?　Did someone dye my hair and dress me like this while I was unconscious? Anyway, curious about what I looked like, I walked over to the mirror in the room. There… stood a guy with blond hair, blue eyes, and a rather unlikable face.

“Who the hell is that?!” That was definitely my first thought… but… I don’t know, it’s a strange feeling—like I’ve seen him before, but maybe not. Who does he look like? He just seems vaguely familiar… To begin with… um, it’s coming back to me, albeit vaguely.

I was an office worker at a “black company”… or so I thought. Could it be that I fell asleep from lack of sleep and drifted into a dream, having some weird dream? I pinched my cheek to check if I was dreaming, but since I felt real pain, I don’t think this is… a dream. Anyway, I don’t really understand it, but there’s no doubt I’ve somehow ended up looking strangely good-looking. At least, it’s different from the appearance I remember having.

Is that it? Is this what they call reincarnation? Even if it’s just a dream, this kind of thing is pretty cool, isn’t it? I should just set aside for now the idea that I’ve possessed someone else’s body or something like that. With that in mind, I fiddle with my body to check my situation further. Anyway, I have to figure out who I’ve become and where I am.

…There’s some kind of whip hanging from my waist… with what looks like a gem attached to the handle. A gem? Oh well, this is kind of in the way, so I’ll just set it aside for now. Just as I tried to let go of the whip… it wouldn’t come off my hand.

Huh? Wait… what is this whip? Is it some kind of cursed weapon or something!? I swung it over and over, trying to get it off my hand, but it just wouldn’t let go. What’s going on? As I was thinking that, I noticed an icon in the corner of my vision.

I vaguely focused my attention on that icon, and a status screen popped up instantly. Um, my level is over 300. Is that really high by this world’s standards? And… there’s all kinds of gear and stuff here. That’s when a name popped into my head.
Takt Alsaholn Faubrey

…That’s a name I’m sure I’ve heard somewhere before! Seriously, where was it? No, wait—I feel like it was the name of someone with a really annoying name who used to drive me crazy during my commute, and at the same time, I’d secretly laugh my head off thinking, “Serves you right.” Takt… whip… and on top of that, there were other weapon entries in the stats.
Claws, hammer…

Plus, these three… have “Legendary Weapons” in parentheses next to them. …Now I have a really strong hunch. No, I’m absolutely certain! A blond guy named Takt who uses a whip as his weapon, wearing a jacket and jeans. With a level over 300, it can only be him! As soon as I thought that, vague memories of this body’s original owner gradually began to surface.
Ugh… there’s no doubt about it. There’s no question that I’ve become Takt, the villain from the web novel *The Rise of the Shield Hero*.

*The Rise of the Shield Hero*. It’s a work posted on the “Let’s Become a Novelist” website—which I often browse on my phone during my commute—and it even got adapted into an anime. It’s an adventure story about a protagonist named Naofumi Iwatani, who was reading a book in the library and was summoned as the Shield Hero depicted in the *Book of the Four Holy Weapons*. While getting summoned was a good thing, he ends up enduring all sorts of terrible ordeals from the very beginning, but uses his frustration as fuel to fight back against the injustices he faces. It’s also a story set in a world teeming with enemies—from the other three heroes, who rejoiced at being summoned into a game world but then conspire against and persecute him simply because he’s the Shield Hero, to a religious cult that seeks to torment him.

I’ve been following the series since pretty early on, getting angry at the unfair situations at times, feeling sad at others, and taking joy in seeing the protagonist overcome those injustices and defeat the villains. Some say it’s a revenge story, while others say it’s a rags-to-riches tale. Personally, what made me laugh was an acquaintance who mocked the story, saying something like, “You die just from reading a book and get reincarnated?” When I pointed out that getting summoned while reading a book is actually a pretty old trope in fantasy, he turned bright red and snapped back at me. In any case, there’s no doubt this is a work that divides opinion.

So… wasn’t *The Rising of the Shield Hero* the series that ran daily for a full year before wrapping up? A while after that, following a side story, the spin-off *The Spear Hero’s Redo* began. It’s the story of the Spear Hero—who was originally just a foil—who, after realizing he’d been deceived by that awful woman Bitch, whom he’d trusted, and falling into a slump, gets encouraged by Filo, the mascot and heroine, and goes on a rampage, eventually becoming the protagonist himself.

It started as a side story posted as an April Fools’ joke but became an official spin-off. The story begins with the Spear Hero, Motoyasu Kitamura, having been defeated by the final boss of *The Shield Hero* and sent into a parallel world where he’s stuck in a loop—but this time, he starts the story in his powerful pre-loop state. Personally, I think this one has a lighter tone and is easier to read. In *The Spear Hero*, the protagonist goes to great lengths to help Naofumi Iwatani—the main character of the main series—and reunite with a girl named Filo.

Anyway… it seems I’ve… reincarnated as a character named Takt, the villain who rose to power in *The Shield Hero*. I’ve reincarnated into a character who’s supposed to be a “reincarnated person”—so what the heck am I, exactly? Some jerk with a bad personality reincarnated into Takt, and then I reincarnated into that same Takt… the very concept of “reincarnation” is starting to make no sense at all. I should stop thinking about this.

Well, I don’t exactly pride myself on being quick to switch gears… but yeah. I should probably think this through a bit. Um… oh, the time until the wave arrives is displayed. I guess I just need to do various things, like strengthening myself, within that time frame.

But you know… Takt is the Whip Hero, but since he’s not the official wielder, he can’t really bring out the weapon’s full potential at all. He’s a foolish guy whose only tactic is brute force relying on his high level, and his end isn’t exactly a pretty one. Seriously… if this is true, there’s nothing but despair. Anyway, I need to check things out first. The vague memories of being Takt that keep popping into my head are too hazy to make sense of. Maybe if I react to something, I’ll be able to remember.
With that in mind, I left the room and walked through the mansion. Then, a beautiful girl in a maid’s uniform noticed me and called out.
“Takt, is something wrong?”
“No, just taking a little walk.”
"Right. Then I'll go with you."
Um… oh, I think I get it. This maid is a girl named Ellie who works for Takt. Huh… she's actually pretty cute. Oh? Her background is coming back to me, too.

As a child, she was the daughter of a local noble… a strong-willed, obnoxious brat with Trash parents… She secretly worked to expose her family’s crimes, leading to their downfall, then won them over by showing a compassionate side and trained them… I’ve even heard she used her power to kill a child from the local territory right from the start. Even in a medieval-style world, she’s a pretty brutal, rotten-blooded girl, isn’t she? I can’t believe they made someone like this the heroine!

Plus, she’s just one of many heroines, she doesn’t feel the slightest guilt about her misdeeds, and she’s got this “Leave the scheming to me” attitude. Still, she’s absolutely loyal—not to me, but to Takt. Lately, though, she’s starting to get bored with him and is asserting herself more, so we’re just going through the motions… I know Takt is a lowlife himself, but no matter how cute she is, my “pretty girl sensor” doesn’t register a single reaction to her. I mean, she’s the “True Spear Hero” who yells things like “Buhito!”

Still… I’d be in trouble if she got suspicious. We’re together all the time, so if she realized I’m not who I seem to be and killed me, that’d be the end of me. Is it too risky to turn her down right now?
“Ah, well… I’d rather not deal with the crowds today. How about just the two of us, Ellie? Let’s go for a walk.”
I said this, trying to act as much like Takt as possible. Ellie blushed and nodded, looking a little shy.
“Takt… I understand. Everyone’s over there, so let’s go out the back.”
“Yeah.”
So, with Ellie leading the way, I slipped out of the mansion… and started walking toward the town of Faubrey. I have the map memorized. It’s a big help that I know the layout so well.

From there, I walked with Ellie through the streets of this otherworldly town, trying to keep things as natural as possible… but then Ellie wrapped her arm around mine. Hmm… her chest is pressing against me, and at this angle, she’s touching my… sensitive area too. Hey, Takt, do you always walk like this with girls?! That’s gross! Even if you’re a womanizer, you should at least think about how you look to others!
“Where are we going?”
“How about the shooting range? Let’s take care of those guys we caught. You said you wanted to blow off some steam, didn’t you?”

…Why can’t you come up with anything but such gory suggestions? I know that “taking care of those guys we caught” at the shooting range isn’t a normal thing to do, no matter how you look at it. Plus, judging by the flow of the conversation, this seems like something she does on a regular basis. I don’t want a heroine who does stuff like that all the time… No, does Takt really not realize this? Well, since she’s an antagonist in *The Shield Hero*, maybe her character is just exaggerated to the extreme. I hope that’s the case. Or else it just means Takt is that much of a scumbag.
“I’m not in the mood for that right now. Maybe we should go grocery shopping or something.”
“Really? What should we buy…? How about we kill a fresh Filolial from the market and make some fried chicken?　It tastes better if you make them suffer a lot before killing them, doesn’t it?”

Filolials are bird-like monsters in this world that pull carriages, and characters like Filo—the heroine of *The Shield Hero*—belong to that species. I’ve heard some are eaten, but… uh, this is bad. Just hearing “Filolial cuisine” makes me think of *The Spear Hero*. “Making them suffer first”? If this were a spin-off, they’d be killed in a way even worse than when their eggs were cracked.
…I’ve completely lost my appetite. I don’t want to die, so I can’t eat a Filolial. Absolutely not.

But what the hell is up with these guys? They’re even worse than how they’re portrayed in *The Shield Hero* series. Just because they’re enemy characters doesn’t mean they should torture a living creature before strangling it—what kind of mindset do they have?
“Come to think of it…”

Even if it feels unnatural, I’d better take the lead in this conversation or things might get ugly. No, wait—Takt is a pretty whimsical guy, so even if I say something weird out of the blue, he might accept it to some extent. After all, he suddenly started talking about a “slow life” and bought a deserted island to develop, and he’s been making “corporate slave drinks” in Shieldfreeden under the guise of “domestic policy cheats.”
“So, these ‘waves’ have started happening—but were the Legendary Four Holy Heroes actually summoned?”

“I heard that pig and the folks from other countries are holding a meeting to summon them, right? Aren’t they still in the middle of planning the ritual? I thought they were currently gathering representatives from each country.”

Ah… If I recall correctly, according to the backstory of *The Rising of the Shield Hero*, Faubrey was supposed to be leading the effort to summon them. But in the middle of that, Melromarc beats them to it and performs the summoning. That fact doesn’t become widely known until a little later. Since Ellie should be answering my question based on what she knows, the timing must be before the Heroes are summoned… right? Yeah, that’s the early part of *The Rise of the Shield Hero*.
At that thought, a chill ran down my spine, and a cold sweat broke out.
Is the world I’m in right now the world of *The Rise of the Shield Hero*? Or is it the world of *The Spear Hero’s Redo*? No… it might actually be the world of *The True Spear Hero’s Redo*.

If it’s *The Rise of the Shield Hero*, that’s still better. Takt just ends up getting his comeuppance in the end, and since I’ve read the original work, there might be ways for me to survive by defusing various foreshadowing flags… maybe.

At the very least, I want to cut ties with the members of Takt’s harem. Not a single one of them has a decent background or personality. After all, we’ve seen plenty of that in *The Spear Hero* and *The True Spear Hero*. To be blunt, even in Takt’s current memories, these women are so deranged that it’s presumptuous to even call them heroines. They’re the kind of people who, in high-pitched voices, suggest they want to watch people get killed or see guts splatter everywhere. If you have even a shred of sanity, you’d want to keep your distance from them. I don’t even want to think about the fact that people like this are living normal lives and blending into the world. That’s why Takt thinks this:
“Since I was reincarnated, the world has been gradually getting better.”
You’ve got to be kidding me. It’s just convenient for you, isn’t it?

Still… it’s true that they’re a nuisance because they’re in a position to fully leverage Takt’s background and authority… I’ll have to handle them skillfully, though. What I have to be careful about is that if the Four Holy Heroes find out I’m a reincarnated person and expose the mastermind or my true circumstances, it’ll be dangerous. It seems some kind of “bomb” like that has been planted on reincarnated people, and several have died in the story. The fact that something similar has been planted on Takt… should have been revealed in the book version.

However, since Takt already holds that position… there’s still a way out if I cooperate with the Heroes without revealing the inside story—just making it look like I’m cooperating even though I can’t actually tell them the truth. It’s like this… I’ll just send that worthless woman the Heroes seem likely to beat, and have them take them out one by one. You know, the one who’s like the weakest of the Four Heavenly Kings… or something like that.
Wait, hold on!
This is a pretty underhanded plan. Let’s not do it. It’s totally in line with Takt’s nature. You shouldn’t let your memories blend into my personality.

I guess this is something I’ll have to handle myself… for the sake of the world. Maybe I should fight a strong opponent to weaken their forces or something… It’d be great if he’d reform, but he doesn’t seem like the type. If I go with the “Let’s cooperate with the Heroes!” approach, I feel like I’d end up running amok at the worst possible moment—or slip up and end up as enemies anyway.

For now, I should probably stop thinking about this scenario based on the premise that it’s *The Rising of the Shield Hero*. Instead, let’s consider the case where it’s a redo of *The Spear Hero* or *The True Spear Hero*.

That’s the worst-case scenario. The Spear Hero is far stronger than me right from the start of the loop. Even if I mobilized all the women, I wouldn’t stand a chance. He’s a monster I absolutely cannot defeat in a straightforward fight. To win, I’d have to be truly recognized by this Sacred Weapon I’m holding.

But… as I am now, no matter what I do, the Whip isn’t accepting the enhancements based on my knowledge of the original story. Seriously, the enhancements just aren’t working… I’ve gotten a little stronger, but… it’s painfully obvious that I can’t enhance it properly. So this is what it means to not be recognized by a weapon…

Early on in the “Spear Hero’s Redo,” since Motoyasu Kitamura’s memories of Takt are vague, if I try to get along with him before we become enemies… and become friends with the “Shield Hero,” there’s a high chance he’ll listen to me. But… after that, it’s the worst-case scenario. He’ll undoubtedly use every trick in the book to eliminate Takt.

That said… up until the Melromarc arc, it’s still possible—just barely—to establish a cooperative relationship with Naofumi through discussion. However, if it’s after that, the Faubrey Pig King will rat him out for cheating, and he’ll be stripped of his weapon and executed. He’ll be dealt with in a single sentence. And if he’s the True Spear Hero… that’s bad. Really bad.

Just like in some mystery story, you’d be forced to endure a terrifying ordeal on a deserted island! Even if you know who the culprit is, you can’t do anything about it—what kind of hell is that?! Monsters straight out of a splatter horror movie would come after you. “Can you survive?” Of course not! It’s total annihilation!

Even if you somehow managed to avoid that… there’s no doubt the Spear Hero would come out of hiding and do everything in his power to hunt me down. Being targeted by a killer I absolutely can’t beat is the absolute worst! The best thing to do is ditch this weapon, change my face, hair color, and name, and make a clean getaway! It’d be great if I could switch bodies using a homunculus or something…
But… even if I tried something like that… there’s a high chance the women from the harem would come after me.

Why did I have to end up as Takt, of all things! Well, I guess it might be better than becoming Bitch, aka the Crimson Swine. That guy’s got a death sentence hanging over his head. If I’m going to become something anyway… assuming I can’t be one of the Heroes… since I’m a guy, I’d rather be the old man who runs the weapon shop!

All I’d have to do is be nice to the Shield Hero, and if I work as a blacksmith, I’d probably manage just fine, right? I’ve been reading books where all sorts of mysteries are being revealed. Whether it’s a shield or a spear, it’s a position where I could get by reasonably well. If I were a girl, would Elena be the safest bet? It’d be nice to be raised as a Filolial Spear Hero while being a background character. Just being around him would get me by to some extent. I’d just have to go on saying “Filololon” or something, right?

But… in this world, we don’t see any reincarnated monsters, do we…? Given the typical pattern of the posting sites where this is published, it wouldn’t be strange if they existed. Yet, as things stand, there aren’t any. It feels like there might be some hidden backstory. It’s the kind of series where discarded concepts and such get revealed, after all… At most, there’s only that one girl, but she’s an ally. To begin with, given the nature of the hosting site, I don’t think it’s treated as a “monster reincarnation” story.

Anyway… what matters is whether it’s a shield, a spear, or a True Spear. Can’t I get to Melromarc with a weapon like a whip…? At worst, if I can stop the summoning, my chances of survival will skyrocket.

Damn… nothing! The closest option is probably Zeltoble. Even then, it’ll take a few days. But if I went by plane or something, I’d stand out too much. Besides, this world wasn’t really suited for airplanes to begin with. …There’s a way to figure out whether it’s a shield or a spear right here.
“Takt, where are you going?”
After finishing our walk and grocery run and dropping Ellie off at the mansion, I turned my back and started walking away.
“Just running an errand at the castle. Don’t follow me. I don’t really like it when people are too clingy, you know?”

If I don’t reject her with this brusque attitude, she’ll definitely follow me. Still, just to be safe, I decided to activate a cloaking-like skill—called “Cloking”—that was inside my whip to shake off any pursuers. Ugh… I can’t use this for very long. Even though that “Spear Hero” guy uses it all the time.

Combined with my magic… it’d be easier to just use magic normally… but I can only cast up to “Drifa.” I’m not exactly sure what Takt’s magical affinity is, but I should be able to use fire magic, so I’ll manage. Anyway, I managed to shake off any potential pursuers and made it to the castle.
“Hey.”
“Well, well, Lord Takt. What brings you here today?”
I called out to the receptionist at the castle. This time… it looks like a soldier under my influence.
“I’ve got a quick question.”
“What might that be?”

“I’m pretty sure there’s a gathering of leaders from various countries coming up, right? So, do you happen to know where the Queen of Melromarc is right now? Even if it’s just a rumor, tell me anything—no matter how small.”
I asked the castle receptionist as naturally as possible, pretending to be thinking of that Bitch.
“Please wait a moment.”

The soldier, as if answering my question, led me deeper into the castle to inquire. I was shown into a private room, so I sat down on a chair for the time being… but that Takt guy—maybe it’s just a habit—was sitting with his legs crossed so arrogantly that even I was surprised. “Sit with a little more class,” I thought to myself, and consciously sat down normally. About ten minutes later… the soldier hurried into the room.
“Excuse me.”
“Ah.”
What is this…? I felt a wave of unbearably unpleasant sweat run down my spine.

“Well… I’ve been instructed to handle this matter as peacefully as possible, but there are conflicting reports that he’s been led away by someone claiming to be the ‘Spear Hero.’ It’s likely a rumor, but since I was told to report even the smallest detail, I’m bringing this to your attention.”
It was the Spear!!! AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH! I’m going to be brutally slaughtered—!
And it’s the later part, right?! No doubt about it! It’s gotta be at least the second half of Zeltoble or later, isn’t it AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!?

I don’t know if it’s one of my many playthroughs or if that guy got stuck in a loop during the early stages of *True: The Spear Hero*, but what the hell is going to happen to me after this, AAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAAH!
April Fools' Day
